case_title: Rohit Bishnoi v. State of Rajasthan & Anr.
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute: the victim was in an extra-marital live-in relationship with a woman who was the sister-in-law of the accused, and accused allegedly threatened him by calls and WhatsApp messages
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.120B; Arms Act s.3 r/w ss.25 and 27
weapon: Country-made pistol (struck with butt; bullets fired)
evidence_type: Eyewitness and identification evidence, CCTV footage, recovery of weapons and phones, call tower records, reconnaissance details (as relied on by the State; the Court noted adequate material prima facie)
aggravating_circumstances: Alleged honour killing; alleged conspiracy plus active participation in the murder; specific roles ascribed to each accused
trial_court_outcome: No verdict; trial pending. Sessions court dismissed Vikas Vishnoi's regular bail application on 10 November 2021
high_court_outcome: Bail granted: Vikas Vishnoi on 14 February 2022; Budharam and Rajendra Bishnoi on 2 February 2023
neutral_facts: The victim, a 25-year-old man, was in a live-in relationship with a married woman whose family members were reported to be unhappy about it. Family members allegedly threatened the victim by calls and WhatsApp messages. On 17 May 2020 a relative told the victim's brother that a video of the victim being shot was circulating on social media. The victim was found dead on the ground in a local area, with blood near his ribs. According to the informant, four persons arrived on two motorcycles, dragged the victim, who was buying vegetables, and shot him. The chargesheet describes specific roles: one accused pulled the victim's collar from behind to drag him down stairs, another held him, a third struck his head with the butt of a pistol, and a fourth fired bullets into his chest and back. Investigators collected statements from eyewitnesses and other witnesses who identified the accused in photographs and CCTV footage showing them leaving the scene. Police reportedly recovered weapons, phones used to transmit information, call tower records and motorcycles. Material on how the victim and the woman were traced and on reconnaissance before the incident was also placed on record.
physical_harm: Death by gunshot wounds to chest and back; head struck with pistol butt
number_of_offences: 5 charged (IPC s.302, s.120B, Arms Act s.3, s.25, s.27); 0 finally upheld (bail matter, no conviction)
premeditation_planning: Not finally found; the Court noted prima facie material on reconnaissance and tracing before the incident
motive: alleged: Family anger over the victim's extra-marital live-in relationship (honour killing)
key_evidence_accepted: Not decided on merits. The Court held there was adequate prima facie material, including details of tracing, pre-incident reconnaissance and each accused's participation
witness_credibility: Not assessed on merits. The Court said a witness turning hostile is not a factor to weigh in bail and that the risk of witness influence could not be ruled out
custody_duration: Arrested 22 May 2020 (Budharam) and 30 May 2020 (Rajendra Bishnoi, Vikas Vishnoi); remanded to judicial custody. Total duration not stated
bail_history: Vikas Vishnoi: Sessions bail dismissed 10 Nov 2021; High Court bail withdrawn 16 Apr 2021; High Court bail granted 14 Feb 2022. Budharam and Rajendra Bishnoi: High Court bail granted 2 Feb 2023
trial_duration: offence: 17 May 2020; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 14 February 2022 and 2 February 2023; Supreme Court: 24 July 2023
legal_representation: Accused (respondents): Asad Alvi, Hamid Irfan, Nishant Bishnoi, Srishti Prabhakar and others. State: B.S. Rajesh Agrajit. Appellant: Pradeep Chhindra, Rajan Chawla
investigation_status: FIR registered; chargesheet filed 19 August 2022; trial pending
procedural_irregularity: High Court granted bail by cryptic and casual orders without reasons and without considering material aspects of the case
appeal_history: Trial court: bail dismissed (10 Nov 2021). High Court: bail granted (14 Feb 2022 and 2 Feb 2023). Supreme Court: appeals allowed, High Court orders set aside, bail cancelled
prosecution_argument: Overwhelming evidence (eyewitnesses, CCTV, recoveries, call records, reconnaissance) prima facie shows guilt; accused conspired and actively participated; bail should be cancelled
defence_argument: Trial will take long, so prolonged custody is unjust; no real risk of witness influence since accused were in custody when the witness turned hostile; no bail misuse; individual roles denied
legal_principle_applied: Bail factors (seriousness, flight risk, witness impact, tampering) must be weighed; prima facie view must be reasoned; casual, cryptic bail orders are liable to be set aside under Article 136
precedent_relied_upon: Gudikanti Narasimhulu (1978) 1 SCC 240; Prahlad Singh Bhati (2001) 4 SCC 280; Anil Kumar Yadav (2018) 12 SCC 129; Ram Govind Upadhyay (2002) 3 SCC 598; Prasanta Kumar Sarkar (2010) 14 SCC 496; Ramesh Bhavan Rathod (2021) 6 SCC 230; Manoj Kumar Khokhar (2022 SCC OnLine SC 30); Jaibunisha (2022) 5 SCC 465; Brijmani Devi (2022) 4 SCC 497; Deepak Yadav (2022) 8 SCC 559
judicial_aggravating_factors: Seriousness of allegations; alleged honour killing; prima facie specific roles in the murder; risk of witness influence and evidence tampering
other_sentence_order: Bail bonds cancelled; accused directed to surrender within two weeks
